> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d6de8e609febc89ec06ab2246fca297ab14a0a8` — the merge of head `8f838b7460d216f7d8a18c9bdff2e11995368fed` into base `99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d6de8e609febc89ec06ab2246fca297ab14a0a8 && git checkout 3d6de8e609febc89ec06ab2246fca297ab14a0a8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f 8f838b7460d216f7d8a18c9bdff2e11995368fed && git checkout -B drift-repro 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f && git merge --no-ff 8f838b7460d216f7d8a18c9bdff2e11995368fed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f838b7460d216f7d8a18c9bdff2e11995368fed`
Local-runs: none

Review of PR #23286 (card #23225, ADR-0138 card E2 slice 1: D2 only) at the head above, rendered 2026-10-13T14:41Z inside the adopting seat's session by an isolated read-only reviewer. Inputs: the card's body and every comment (triage `6144040679`, claim `6144558082`, the cross-lane declaration `6144567590` on #6367, the dev's `os-dev-report` `6147723822`, and the seat's ACCEPT `6147845189`, read as a claim to test), ADR-0138 on `origin/main`, the PR's body, title, file list and net diff against the merge base `09ef77c7d8`, the head's own files where the diff lacked context, and the head's check-runs. Not an input: the dispatch order or the seat's conclusions. The card is `security`, so this record stays at function level: function, file and decision names only.

**Check-runs on the head**, latest run per name, read 2026-10-13T14:40Z after four polls over ten minutes: every concluded run is `success` or `skipped`, with no failure; Test Core shards 1 to 4 of 6 were still `in_progress` (shards 5 and 6 concluded `success`), and this record judges on what has concluded. A green head is the queue's own separate condition, which the seat reads before landing. `Check Changeset` (three runs, the last on the corrected title), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · workspace`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and the four PR-shape checks are green. Two facts about what the check-runs do not cover: the `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards are skipped on every `pull_request` event by the workflow's own condition, and Test Core runs with `--exclude @objectstack/dogfood`, so no check-run on this head executes `authz-conformance.test.ts`, `authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` or `anonymous-door-sweep.dogfood.test.ts`. Their evidence on this head is the dev's local run (3 files, 124 tests) and the dev's four ablations; the first check-run verdict on the matrix block is `main`'s battery after the merge, which is where ADR-0138 criterion 2 places the sweep by design. I read the test code itself and judge it below on that reading.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged.

**The three floors: right.** In `keys.ts` (`handleKeysRequest`), `notifications.ts` (`handleNotificationRequest`) and `share-links.ts` (`handleShareLinksRequest`), the first statement is now the shared decision `shouldDenyAnonymous` from `@objectstack/core`, before `deps.resolveService`, `deps.getObjectQL` or `deps.getRequestKernelService` is called and before any face or verb is selected; the new unit suite `domain-floor-anonymous-deny.test.ts` asserts, for both anonymous shapes the dispatcher produces (an unresolved context and the D9 guest envelope), that none of the three seams is called (`expectNothingResolved`). Each refusal is `deps.error(ANONYMOUS_DENY_MESSAGE, ANONYMOUS_DENY_STATUS, { code: ANONYMOUS_DENY_CODE })`, character for character the spelling `actions.ts`, `automation.ts`, `analytics.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `packages.ts` and `ai.ts` use, so the wire body is the dispatcher's standard wrapper with the shared message. No second spelling survives: the three domain-local messages the base carried are gone; the `|| !ec || !ec.userId` arm in `keys.ts`, the `|| !userId` arm in `notifications.ts` and the body-level `!ec?.userId` arm in `handleShareLinksRequestBody` are tautologies of the floor (with no `method`, `path` or `isSystem` passed, `shouldDenyAnonymous({ userId })` is exactly `!userId`), each spelled with the same three constants and each documented as a compiler narrowing rather than a decision. One deliberate difference from the six sibling floors, named rather than hidden: the siblings pass `isSystem` and `method` (and `automation.ts` the path); these three pass the user id alone. That is the base's own behaviour for these domains (judged under the census below), and it means the OPTIONS arm of the shared decision does not apply here, which changes nothing: none of the three domains ever admitted an anonymous OPTIONS before (no face took it), so that answer moves from the 405 or the capability answer to the 401, inside the disclosed change.

For `/share-links`, exactly the two class-2 token faces are exempt: `isPublicShareLinkRoute` admits a GET whose sub-path has exactly two segments ending in `resolve` or `messages`, and `handleShareLinksRequestBody` selects its two public arms with the identical predicate shape (the same leading-slash strip, split and filter, segment count and verb), so every request the exemption admits is served by a token face and judged by `svc.resolveToken`, and no management face (zero segments, or one segment under DELETE) and no path the domain does not serve can reach it: a two-segment path under any verb but GET, or a `resolve`/`messages` segment at any other depth, falls to the floor (case B of the suite pins a selection of these; case E pins both token faces admitted with the service asked about the token). A new public face would need an edit to that predicate, which the file's header and the matrix row both name as an amendment of ADR-0138, never an edit alone. A note for the seat, not a defect: ADR-0138 D2's table names `registerShareLinkRoutes` (plugin-sharing) as class 2's enforcer; the dispatcher twin's two token faces are the same door on the transport cloud's per-environment kernels serve, unobservable on the showcase boot, so their admission is pinned by the unit suite's case E alone, as the matrix row says.

No signed-in caller's answer changes: case D of the suite pins, for each domain, that a member reaches every face with the same service calls (`listInbox` with the member's id; the 405 for a wrong verb and the data-service probe on the mint; `createLink`, `listLinks` with `createdBy` the member, `revokeLink`) and still gets the capability answer where the slot is empty. The diff removes no signed-in branch and reorders none that reads the user: the inbox probe and the method check now sit after the floor, which a caller carrying a user id passes.

**The system-context census: right.** At the merge base all three domains already required a user id: `keys.ts` refused `!ec || !ec.userId` (after its method check), `notifications.ts` refused `!userId` (after its inbox probe), and the management faces of `share-links.ts` refused `!ec?.userId` (after the service probe); none had an `isSystem` arm. So a system or service caller without a user id never reached a face in any of the three before, and asking about the user id alone denies no caller that was admitted before; a caller with a user id passes the floor exactly as it passed the old check. Nothing is admitted that should not be: the floor admits only a truthy `userId`, the same predicate as before. The dev's record that passing the system flag turned `check:system-context-census` red (three new elevation read sites with no behaviour behind them) is the right reason to keep the flag out, and that gate is what reds if someone later adds it. One gap, stated: no case in the suite drives an `isSystem: true` context with no user id through a floor, so "refused exactly as before" for that shape rests on the code reading above rather than on a pin; it is held structurally (the floor, then each file's narrowing arm) and is not a reason to fail.

**The six class rows: right.** Each row names D2's enforcing site by the function D2's table names, and each symbol exists at this head: `RestServer.registerFormEndpoints` (`rest-server.ts`) and the `publicFormGrant` branch of `SecurityPlugin` (class 1); `registerShareLinkRoutes` (`share-link-routes.ts`, class 2); `isPublicAudienceRead` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`, class 3); `resolveExecutionContext` (`resolve-execution-context.ts`) and the CRUD gate (class 4), then `@objectstack/service-automation` (class 5); `registerStorageRoutes` and `authorizeDownload` (`storage-routes.ts`, class 6). Each row is `enforced`, HIGH_RISK (the six ids are spread into `HIGH_RISK`), and cites `anonymous-door-sweep.dogfood.test.ts`, which now claims exactly the six by `authz-row:` lines, so `checkLedger`'s mutual attribution holds in both directions. The sweep asserts each class on a real subject, admitted and refused, in its own `describe` per class: class 1 admits resolve and submit of a form declaring anonymous sharing and refuses an undeclared slug; class 2 admits a minted token to its one record and refuses it revoked; class 3 admits the public book, its tree and a doc it claims and refuses a non-public book and a write; class 4 asserts the engine is asked once with the guest envelope and answers D3's empty-state refusal, and refuses the session-gated sibling; class 5 asserts the flow runs once as the guest and serves its output only, and refuses the sibling; class 6 serves a `public_read` file's bytes at both download doors and refuses a private file at both. Removing a site's admission reds the admitted leg (the dev's ablation of `isPublicAudienceRead` turned exactly class 3's two admitted legs red, 2 of 20), and removing its refusal reds the refused leg of the same case. The closed-list block in `authz-conformance.test.ts` is a vitest block, not a gate script: `checkDoorClassList` reds a row carrying the `anonymous-door-` prefix outside the six (a seventh), a listed id with no row (a missing row, which also orphans the sweep's claim in `checkAuthzLedger`), a row that is not `enforced`, one that cites another proof or none (which the ledger also reds as a high-risk row without proof and as non-mutual attribution), one that is not HIGH_RISK, and one whose enforcement text stops naming its D2 site (the reworded control); a renamed id is caught twice, as a missing listed id and as an unlisted prefixed id, and a rename that drops the prefix is caught as missing. No new gate script: confirmed on the file list.

**The new-route pin: right.** The dispatcher-domain ledger key is minted by the probe over `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`, one key per domain prefix inside `ROUTE_LEDGER`, so a route added inside an existing domain mints no key (the dev's scratch ablation 4 re-measured it: zero UNCLASSIFIED, only the docblock row-count pin moved) while a new domain or REST family does (ablation 3: UNCLASSIFIED red). Inside a domain the only hold is the floor being the first statement, which the matrix now pins three ways: the GATE_PIN probes on the three domain files mint `notifications:domains/notifications.ts:anonymous-gate`, `keys:domains/keys.ts:anonymous-gate` and `share-links:domains/share-links.ts:anonymous-gate` only while the call spelling is in the file; the new negative control removes each of the eight `DOMAIN_FLOOR_GATE_KEYS` from the discovered set in turn and asserts `STALE covers` naming that gate (the same effect a deleted call has, which the dev's ablation 2 measured on `notifications.ts`: the covering row STALE, a DEAD PROBE, 9 matrix failures); and a second case asserts the set of minted `:anonymous-gate` keys equals exactly those eight, so a ninth floor cannot arrive unpinned and a pinned floor cannot vanish from the list. Case B of the unit suite closes the loop at the handler: a path or verb no face serves is refused by the floor before route selection, in each of the three domains. The claim is true at this head.

**The census and the baseline: right.** `LEDGER_POPULATION_BASELINE_MAX` 30 to 26, and the four keys that left are `dispatcher-domain:route-ledger.ts:/notifications`, `/keys` and `/share-links` (each covered by its new `anonymous-deny-*` floor row beside its gate-pin key) and `rest-family:rest-route-ledger.ts:forms` (covered by the class 1 row). The three domain keys are exactly what the floors classify. The `forms` key is not a floor's: it leaves because both routes of that family are class 1 doors by declaration (the ledger lists exactly two `family: 'forms'` rows, both `disposition: 'public'`, after the lookup-picker row left earlier), admitted by `registerFormEndpoints`' own sharing-declaration rule and refused for an undeclared slug by the sweep; that is a declared door, not an unguarded surface, and the row's note says why a family key is the one thing a door class can classify. No key left unguarded. The probe census arithmetic holds: 20 to 23 entries (three GATE_PINs), 15 to 18 files, 22 to 29 keys (three gate keys, three domain keys, one family key), `MATRIX_HEADER_PROBE_CLAIM` 23 beside the header's "23 probes over 18 named source files", 65 rows of which 16 carry `covers` (12 before, plus three floors and class 1), 58 `enforced` of which 43 carry none, and 10 gate pins (7 plus three); the population block enumerates the four keys as classified. The census file's per-file controls (`shouldDenyAnonymous(` once; the handler name 2, 4 and 6 times) match the head's files.

**The `assemble-execution-context.ts` doc change: right.** The diff is nineteen lines inside the module's doc comment, no code line, no export: cross-lane as declared on #6367 (`6144567590`). Its text matches D9 (the two named entries, the 2026-08-08 Option A ruling recorded by the ADR) and D2's closure of the adoption rule (six classes in D2's order; the two endpoint classes take the guest envelope, the other four derive their authorization from a declaration, everything else answers 401 decided once per domain; a new door class is an amendment of the record, never a call site; the list is recorded in the conformance matrix). No `@objectstack/core` release is owed: Post-Task Checklist step 3 triggers a changeset for a feature, functional improvement or fix that publishes, and a doc comment is none of those even though the emitted `dist/index.d.ts` carries it; `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head. The dev's phrase "fast track" has no anchor in AGENTS.md; the authority is step 3's own trigger list.

**The five existing tests moved to a signed-in caller: right, with one nuance.** Each keeps its original assertion's meaning: `domain-handler-registry.test.ts` still pins the 405 for a wrong verb on the mint (now through `handleKeys` with a member) and the 501 with no share-link service (through `handleShareLinks` with a member), each with the anonymous 401 and `UNAUTHENTICATED` asserted beside it, and tightens the segment-boundary pin from "not 405" to the 404; `share-links-public-cache-headers.test.ts` still pins that an authenticated route propagates a throw unchanged; `dispatcher-5xx-always-logged.test.ts` still pins that the `/notifications` 501 costs no `error` line; the four boots in `declared-capability-absence-warn-once.test.ts` still pin the once-per-route warn, the dedupe key, the shared envelope predicate and the exact 501 bytes on every request (an instrument that was, and remains, runnable at the base for a signed-in caller); `notification-schema-conformance.test.ts` replaces the pinned message with the code and `httpStatus`, because the message is what this PR unifies, and adds the ordering pin (an empty slot is still 401 to an anonymous caller). The nuance: in three of those files the anonymous 401 is asserted not beside the moved case but in the sibling the comment names, `domain-floor-anonymous-deny.test.ts`, which pins it for every face and both anonymous shapes; that is not a weakened pin, since none of the moved cases pinned anonymity on purpose, and `SIGNED_IN_AUTH` is defined in both boot-based files.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` `minor` with `fix(runtime)!:` as the changeset's summary line and as the PR title (corrected by the seat from a `feat(runtime,dogfood):` spelling), `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body line 2 and in the changeset, one adr-0087 comment marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` stating its facts, and the launch-window BREAKING line: right against Post-Task Checklist step 3 and the two precedents. Step 3's closed pair makes `(narrowing)` BREAKING and demands exactly one ADR-0087 marker in the changeset body; the marker is present, one, and its facts hold (no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition, stored shape or export moves, so nothing for a migration to rewrite; the remedy is to sign in). The migration clause does not apply: nothing an author can write is removed or renamed. PR #23211 and PR #23263 carried `yes (narrowing)` because each also widened an entry (new `@objectstack/rest` exports) beside the runtime narrowing; this diff exports nothing new in any published package, so `no` is the truthful first axis, and `no (narrowing)` is the spelling the gates read: `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0 in the dev's run, and `Check Changeset` is green on the head three times. `minor` for a BREAKING change is the launch-window convention both precedents used.

The tension the dev named: `execution-duties.md` says a runtime permission or security behaviour change is not Clause ② and that pulling back to a declared contract does not touch it, while the claim graded a move that changes an answer as `no (narrowing)` with a review owed. `no (narrowing)` is the right reading of both. Clause ② asks one question, whether the card widens an accept set or expands a public surface, and the answer here is `no` on either text; `execution-duties.md`'s own line on narrowing says a card that narrows a published accept set is `Clause-②: no`, stays in its lane, and owes one contract-tier review before the queue, which is exactly the claim's rule and this record. The `(narrowing)` arm is the level axis, not a second Clause ② answer: it records that a published package's wire answer moves for a caller (the 501 and 405 an anonymous caller used to read, and the three messages, become the shared 401), which a client could observe, so BREAKING under the launch window is the conservative and correct grade; a bare `no` would ship an observable wire change as `patch` with no marker and no review. The measurement that made the arm necessary was the dev's, raised rather than chosen silently, as the claim required.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated.

- **Open question 1, the `/ai` route-level `auth: false` opt-out (`handleAIRequest`, `mountRouteOnServer`).** Right that this slice does not wait: no line of this diff reads or depends on the answer, `/ai` stays in the baseline, its floor is not among the eight gate pins, and the dev measured no in-repo producer. Nothing in the diff is wrong under either answer. Under A (retire the opt-out and move `/ai` to the domain floor), a later slice adds a ninth gate pin and a ninth entry to `DOMAIN_FLOOR_GATE_KEYS`, which the "exactly those eight" case reds until it is updated, the intended ratchet. Under B (a seventh class by amendment), `ADR_0138_D2_DOOR_CLASS_ROWS` grows with the amendment, and `toHaveLength(6)`, the matrix header, the doc comment in `assemble-execution-context.ts` and the sweep's classification move together, which is what "the row follows the amendment, never the reverse" means. Escalation, stated: as of this reading no `needs-user-decision` card for this question is on the repository (the only decision card filed today, #23266, is E1's row-scope question), so the seat's "goes to the maintainer as asked" is an act still owed, not one done; it does not block this PR.

- **Open question 2, REST families.** The seat's reading A holds on ADR-0138's text. D2 states the domain-level decision in terms of the runtime face ("the envelope the runtime face assembles for every sessionless request (D9) is refused in every domain"), the enforcement map says `shouldDenyAnonymous` "at each domain's entry", and the record uses "family" for the REST side throughout criterion 2 (the settings REST family, three families outside the list), naming the metadata family's guarded registrar as the REST shape where one exists. So "domain" in D2 is the dispatcher domain, and the REST families stay per route by construction (each handler opens with `enforceAuth`), held by the booted sweep's everything-else class and the probe census. The claim's file surface allowed `packages/rest`, so the dev measured it and raised it rather than moving it; a family-wide guarded registrar (B) is its own card with its own measurement, as the seat said.

- **The deferred `handleUiRequest` and `handleDataRequest` moves.** Carrying them on #23225 as the next slice, ahead of D2b, is right under Prime Directive #10. The E2 row's own words are "any face of a listed domain that still decides per face moved to the domain-level deny", so both moves are E2's deliverable, not scope expansion, and a separate card would split one record's execution card; the claim deferred the two files to #23214 slice 1, which landed as `d45d0e938a`, so nothing holds them now. The `handleUiRequest` reading is a possible disclosure, read at unit level and not reproduced, so noting it at function level in the report and the ACCEPT is the directive's second clause. The condition, stated: if the reach measurement the seat ordered reproduces it, that is a reproducible defect and the directive's first clause then requires a `security` card, at function level, beside the slice that fixes it.

- **The deviations.** (a) The root pid file `/build-closure.pid` is outside the repository (not on the file list; the repository is identical to before minus the intended changes, Post-Task Checklist step 7), and its deletion is the seat's or a person's; recorded. (b) The five tests moved to a signed-in caller: judged right above. (c) The census, its test and the population baseline edited as the matrix's companions: required, since the three gate pins and the four classified keys move the census figures and the shrink-only baseline, and every figure reconciles (above); inside the claimed `packages/qa/dogfood/test/` surface. (d) Zero label writes: consistent with the dispatch's write budget, and with a changeset added, so `skip-changeset` does not apply.
